title: Invited Research Methodology Mentoring Session (UROG, GIKI)
description:
Undergraduate Research Opportunities at GIKI (UROG) brings you Session 3 of our Research Excellence Series, focused on helping you design a solid research methodology from the ground up.

Join us with PhD student at Texas A&M University (GIKI Batch 27, MS @ Georgia Southern University, PhD @ Texas A&M University), whose work spans machine learning, CFD, and advanced engineering systems.

In this session, you’ll learn how to choose the right research approach, whether it’s surveys, experiments, or simulations, and how to design a clear, step-by-step methodology. We’ll also touch on data ethics, bias, and how to keep your research realistic and feasible.

By the end, you’ll have a defined research objective and a practical methodology plan you can actually follow.

A short hands-on practice session will be held at the end, so keep your laptops ready.

title: ASME IMECE 2025 Presentation on Graph Neural Networks for Thermal-Fluid Modeling
description:
This week, I had the honor of attending the ASME (The American Society of Mechanical Engineers) IMECE 2025 in Memphis, Tennessee. It was a privilege to present my research on the application of graph neural networks for heat transfer and fluid flow problems—a topic that continues to open new possibilities in computational modeling and scientific machine learning.

I am grateful for the opportunity to share my work with distinguished researchers, learn from insightful presentations, and engage in meaningful discussions that will guide the next steps in my research journey. My sincere appreciation goes to my advisor Dr. N. K. Anand, and J. Mike Walker '66 Department of Mechanical Engineering at Texas A&M University for their support.

It was inspiring to be part of such a vibrant engineering community. I look forward to contributing further to the integration of machine learning with computational fluid dynamics, developing models that enhance predictive accuracy, generalizability, and reduce computational cost.

title: ESSCI Technical Meeting: Four Fire and Combustion Modeling Presentations
description:
This week, our team (Shehzad Khan, Muhammad Hasnain, Usman Khan) had the incredible opportunity to attend the Technical Meeting of the Eastern States Section of The Combustion Institute (ESSCI) at The University of Georgia, Athens, US. 

At ESSCI, we presented four conference papers focusing on fire safety and combustion. The following presentations at this prestigious conference were the result of collaboration between Georgia Southern University, Worcester Polytechnic Institute, West Virginia University, North Carolina State University, and Eastern Kentucky University. 

1. Three-Dimensional Mathematical Modeling of Heat and Mass Transfer during Calcination of Gypsum Board Exposed to Fire
2. Mathematical Modeling of Heat-Induced Decomposition Kinetics Leading to Thermal Runaway in Lithium-ion Batteries
3. Mathematical Model for Predicting Injuries and Temperature Distributions in Stem Exposed to Fire
4. Numerical Modeling of Spontaneous Ignition in Large Coal Stockpiles using Finite Volume Method

We thank Albert Simeoni, Shijin Kozhumal, MUTHU KUMARAN S, Ahmed O Said, Reza Ziazi, Ph.D., V'yacheslav (Slava) Akkerman, Greg Gorbett, Trevor Borth, Rylan Paye, Arafat Idris, Jairo Sebastian Casa, and especially our advisor Dr. Hayri Sezer for their guidance and cooperation throughout this work.  

Special appreciation goes to Craig Harvey Dean College of Engineering and Computing, Department of Mechanical Engineering at Georgia Southern University. 


The Combustion Institute provides a platform to bring together experts from industry, national laboratories, and academia in the field of combustion science and engineering to address current challenges related to sustainable transportation, energy efficiency, emissions mitigation in the atmosphere, fire safety, and advanced propulsion systems by dissemination of state-of-the-art research. 

We look forward to more collaborations and discoveries ahead! #CombustionScience #Engineering #Collaboration #ResearchExcellence #lithiumionbatteries #gypsumboard #coal #mortality

title: Interdisciplinary Research Dialogue on Data and Public Health
description:
From Conventional Meetings to Coffee Chats: A Productive Day with Professor Dr. Gulzar Shah, PhD, MStat, MS., Department Chair at College of Public Health, Georgia Southern University

Gone are the days when students and professors had to meet in stuffy offices. Today, we had the honor of meeting the brilliant Professor Dr. Gulzar Shah over coffee at Starbucks, and it was an incredible experience. Dr. Shah has been an inspiration to us in many ways. His 20 years of interdisciplinary training and work experience in both academia and public health practice agencies is truly inspiring. It is an emotional experience to see someone from your home country achieving such great success.

During our coffee chat, Dr. Shah shared his research interests in data improvement tools, and public health finances, among others, which opened new perspectives for us on combining computational modeling, machine learning, and health sciences. We had a very productive discussion that left us feeling energized and motivated to apply the insights gained to our research work.

I would also like to extend a special thanks to our supervisor, Dr. Hayri Sezer, for his support and cooperation throughout. His village recently was hit by an earthquake, and he is still working hard to help the community with his great skills while giving his students the time and attention they need.

But that's not all, we also had the pleasure of having Shehzad Khan, my friend and research assistant. Shehzad is a social person and more like a business-minded person who always brings a fun element to the conversation. We are thankful to Shehzad for his company and for making the conversation more enjoyable.

In conclusion, I would like to thank Dr. Shah, Dr. Sezer, and Shehzad for their time and effort. Our coffee chat was a great reminder that sometimes unconventional meetings can be the most productive ones.
